newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Delors wins Dutch prize for services to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Delors wins Dutch prize for services to Europe.

text.p: This year's Erasmus Prize for exceptional services to Europe has been awarded to the former European Commission president Jacques Delors, Amsterdam's Praemium Erasmianum Foundation said on Monday.

"The prize has been awarded to Jacques Delors because through his vision and personal enthusiasm he exerted an enormous influence on the process of European unification," the Foundation said in a statement.

Delors' sense of the rich political and cultural histories of the various countries making up the united Europe had enabled him to breathe new life into the European Union at a time when it looked to be stagnating, the foundation said.
The prize, named after the 16th century Dutch humanist scholar and philosopher Desiderius Erasmus, consists of a cash sum of 300,000 guilders ($157,000).
It is awarded each year to a person or institution deemed to have made an important cultural, social, or sociological contribution to the European cause.
Previous winners include Czech president and then-dissident Vaclav Havel, Nazi hunter Simon Wiesenthal, sculptor Henry Moore and Nobel prize-winning Dutch economist Jan Tinbergen.
The awards ceremony will be held in the autumn.
